# TEZAUR 0.5.1

Security and robustness release. It comes from an adversarial review of 0.5.0 (hostile `.bib`/RIS/CSL files, a hostile OAI-PMH archive, hostile documents, a hostile client of `tezaur serve`, hostile drafts for `export`). Nothing changes for honest input: no new command, no new flag, no change of defaults.

## Fixed
- **`tezaur serve` could be crashed by one request.** A request announcing `Content-Length: 99999999999` made the server answer 413 and then abort the whole process ("memory allocation failed"). The cause is in the HTTP library (tiny_http 0.12.0 allocates the announced size when it drops an unread body), so the library is now vendored with a one-line fix (`vendor/tiny_http/PATCHES.md`). Early answers (413, 401, 403) no longer take the server down; a body of more than 1 MiB that was not read closes the connection instead of being drained.
- **`export --to tex`: citation keys and locators were copied into `\cite[...]{...}` unescaped**, so a draft containing `[@k, p. \input{/etc/passwd}]` or a key such as `a}\write18{id}{` produced those commands in the `.tex` file. Keys now keep only characters that are safe in a key; locators are escaped like any other text.
- **Control characters from outside no longer reach your files or terminal.** A NUL, an ESC sequence, a bidi override (U+202E) or a zero-width character in a title, author or key (from a `.bib` you were sent, or from an OAI-PMH archive) was written as it was into BibTeX and RIS output and into warnings. `bib`, `oai -o` and the exports now drop them. Values written to BibTeX have balanced braces (an unbalanced `}` could close its own field and add fields); values written to RIS are one line (a newline could start a new record). Letters, accents, every script, ZWJ and ZWNJ are untouched.
- **`oai`: redirects are followed only to the archive that was named.** Before, up to three redirects were followed to any host, scheme or port, which contradicted "only the archive you name is contacted". Now a redirect to another host, another port, a downgrade from https to http, a URL with credentials, or a non-http scheme is refused. The whole request also has a 300 s limit: a server sending one byte a second used to keep the command running for as long as it liked.
- **`tezaur serve`: a GET no longer creates directories.** `?ws=<new name>` created a folder under `--workspaces` for every new name; now only writes do. Responses carry `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.

## Checked and found sound (no change)
Nested and unbalanced `.bib` input (200 000 levels, 5 MB unclosed), `@string` and `crossref` cycles, 100 000 authors in one entry, NUL and invalid UTF-8; a 24 MB `.bib` with 300 000 entries (6 s, about 1.1 GB of memory); XML entity bombs, 100 000-level XML nesting, 30 MB answers, endless resumption tokens and endless empty pages from an archive; a 3 GB-uncompressed `.docx`, an `.epub` with `../` entries, 500 000-level HTML, a 100 MB single-line text; `ws=` path traversal (`../..`, `/etc`, encoded, backslash, NUL), Host-header rebinding, cross-origin and `Origin: null` POSTs, negative and duplicate `Content-Length`, a 3 MB header.

## Known limits (unchanged, stated honestly)
- `tezaur serve` handles requests one at a time: a client that connects and sends nothing blocks the others until it disconnects. Use it on your own machine or behind a proxy that has timeouts.
- A very large `.bib` costs memory (about 45 times its size).
- Its framing is not blocked (the Docker Desktop extension embeds the page), so `X-Frame-Options` is not set.
- The Windows installer, store submissions and the scoop/winget manifests (still at 0.4.0 with placeholder checksums) are as in 0.5.0.
- The model is yours; TEZAUR verifies citations mechanically, it does not prove claims.

Binaries for Linux, macOS (arm64) and Windows plus a `.deb` and checksums are attached by the release workflow.

# TEZAUR 0.5.1 (română)

Versiune de securitate și robustețe, rezultată dintr-o recenzie adversarială a lui 0.5.0. Pentru intrări oneste nu se schimbă nimic: nicio comandă nouă, niciun flag nou.

## Reparate
- **`tezaur serve` putea fi prăbușit cu o singură cerere.** `Content-Length: 99999999999` făcea serverul să răspundă 413 și apoi să se oprească („memory allocation failed”). Cauza era în biblioteca HTTP (tiny_http 0.12.0), acum inclusă în depozit cu o corecție (`vendor/tiny_http/PATCHES.md`).
- **`export --to tex`: cheile și localizatorii de citare ajungeau neescapați în `\cite[...]{...}`**, deci un draft cu `[@k, p. \input{/etc/passwd}]` producea acele comenzi în `.tex`. Cheile păstrează acum doar caractere sigure, iar localizatorii sunt escapați.
- **Caracterele de control din surse externe nu mai ajung în fișiere sau în terminal** (NUL, secvențe ESC, suprascrieri bidi U+202E, caractere de lățime zero), iar valorile BibTeX au acolade echilibrate, iar cele RIS sunt pe o singură linie. Literele, diacriticele, toate scripturile și ZWJ/ZWNJ rămân neschimbate.
- **`oai`: redirecționările se urmează doar spre arhiva numită** (nu spre altă gazdă, alt port, http după https, URL cu parolă sau altă schemă), iar cererea întreagă are limită de 300 s (un server care trimitea un octet pe secundă o putea ține nelimitat).
- **`tezaur serve`: un GET nu mai creează directoare**, iar răspunsurile au `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` și `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.

## Limite cunoscute (neschimbate)
Serverul `serve` tratează cererile pe rând (un client care se conectează și tace le blochează pe celelalte); un `.bib` foarte mare consumă memorie (de ~45 de ori mărimea lui); cadrarea paginii într-un `iframe` nu e blocată, fiindcă o folosește extensia Docker Desktop; manifestele scoop/winget rămân la 0.4.0 cu sume de control provizorii.
